# Snapshot fixture archives

Small `tar.gz` archives in the shape GitHub serves for `GET /repos/<owner>/<repo>/tarball/<ref>`: every entry sits
under one top-level folder `<repo>-<short sha>/` (here `octo-demo-3f78685/`). They are generated by
`node scripts/make-snapshot-fixtures.mjs` with a hand-written ustar writer, so the hostile entries exist on every
operating system. None of the content comes from a real repository (DEC-03); the commit SHA
`3f786850e387550fdab836ed7e6dc881de23001b` is a made-up value.

| Archive | Contents | Proves |
|---|---|---|
| `normal.tar.gz` | `.rosettaignore`, `README.md`, `src/App.cs`, `src/lib/Util.cs` (4 files, 157 bytes) | RF-122 download, extraction, hash and cache reuse |
| `traversal.tar.gz` | the normal entries plus `octo-demo-3f78685/../../escaped.txt` and the absolute path `/abs/absolute.txt` | RF-122 no file lands outside the snapshot folder |
| `links.tar.gz` | the normal entries plus a symbolic link `link-to-readme -> README.md` and a hard link `hard-readme` | RF-127 links are skipped and counted |
| `oversized.tar.gz` | one 64 KiB file `big.bin` (compresses to under 200 bytes) | RF-127 the byte limit stops the extraction, not the download size |
| `many-entries.tar.gz` | 30 files `f/00.txt` .. `f/29.txt` | RF-127 the entry-count limit |

The redirect-to-another-host case of RF-127 is a behaviour of the fake GitHub server (`tests/support/fake-github.ts`)
and uses `normal.tar.gz`.

Regenerating on another operating system may change one byte of the gzip header (the OS code); the archives are
committed, so this does not matter for the tests.
